resources.string: Selective ion exchange in the distal tubule
Educational model of a normal adult early distal convoluted tubule. Symbols, geometry, and timing are schematic, not personal or measured data. Only selected transport routes are shown.
Tubular fluid flows past the apical face of the lining. The opposite, basolateral face borders tissue fluid. Transport across the lining is different from fluid flowing along the lumen.
The apical sodium-chloride cotransporter (NCC) moves one sodium ion and one chloride ion together from the tubule lumen into the cell.
The pump exchanges in opposite directions

The basolateral sodium-potassium pump uses ATP to move three sodium ions out to the tissue fluid and two potassium ions into the cell per cycle. Keeping sodium low inside the cell helps drive its entry through NCC.
Chloride leaves by a different route
Chloride can leave the cell for the tissue fluid through the basolateral ClC-Kb channel. It does not leave through the sodium-potassium pump.
Salt is reclaimed with little water
Together these routes give a net movement of sodium and chloride from the lumen to tissue fluid. The early distal tubule has low water permeability, so water largely stays in the lumen here.
Physiology of the distal convoluted tubule
Educational cross-section of normal adult bladder urothelium. Shape, spacing, and timing are schematic, not personal or measured data. The model shows the local lining only.
At low filling, the bladder mucosa lies in folds. Dome-shaped umbrella cells face the lumen above layers of intermediate and basal cells.
Folds smooth out as the bladder fills
As the bladder fills, the mucosal folds flatten and the same umbrella cells become broader and flatter. The lining appears thinner without shedding its surface layer.

Tight junctions remain connected between neighboring umbrella cells. Together with the specialized surface membrane, these junctions limit movement from urine into the underlying tissue even as the lining changes shape.
As stretch is relieved after emptying, the umbrella cells regain a domed profile and the mucosa gathers into folds again. The surface remains continuous.
